claims.text: The investigated alloys are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets are governed by interactions between local lattice distortions and dislocation glide.
Changing constituent count changes short-range order.
Changing constituent count changes chemical partitioning.
Short-range order and chemical partitioning influence the interaction between local lattice distortions and dislocation glide.
Local lattice distortions and dislocation density are the structural mediators of the mechanical-property differences.
The proposed comparison is conducted at room temperature under uniaxial tensile loading.
In-situ transmission electron microscopy or atom probe tomography will be used to study the deformation mechanisms.
Quaternary subsets will have 15% higher yield strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Quaternary subsets will have 20% lower ductility than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Ternary subsets will have 10% lower yield strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Ternary subsets will have 15% higher ductility than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to thermomechanically processed alloys containing three to five constituents.
Grain size and precipitates may also influence the mechanical properties.
The hypothesis is falsified if quaternary yield strength is not within 5% of its predicted value or ternary ductility is not within 10% of its predicted value.
